cohort: 1,801 women with a previous caesarean section and 1,801 matched women with a previous vaginal delivery from the IMS Disease Analyzer database in Germany
finding: Women with a previous caesarean section were more likely to have a subsequent caesarean section and experience pregnancy-associated disorders in their subsequent pregnancy compared to women with a previous vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Women with a previous caesarean section were significantly more likely to have a subsequent caesarean section (79.0% vs 9.3%) and less likely to have a single spontaneous vaginal delivery (0.04 OR).
